strip.title: One platform for processes, forms and field work

features.title: Everything your operation needs, in one workspace
features.subtitle: Design the process, build its forms, hand the work to people and field teams, and watch it all happen live — no email chains, no spreadsheets, no chasing for updates.

designer.title: Workflow engine
designer.text: Design workflows on a visual canvas — tasks, decisions, timers, nested activities and integrations — then publish versions that run reliably, with retries, incident handling and a full history.

forms.title: Form engine
forms.text: Build forms without code — text, numbers, dates, choices, files, photos, signatures and locations — with rules that show or require fields. Publish versions and attach them to workflow steps and field tasks.

teams.title: Field teams and tasks
teams.text: Hand each task to the team that covers its territory, then track who has it, when it was filled and why it was returned.

monitoring.title: Live monitoring
monitoring.text: Follow each request on its live workflow graph, watch open, overdue and completed work for every group on the workload dashboard, and pick up incidents the moment they happen.

permissions.title: Dynamic roles and permissions
permissions.text: Choose exactly what each role can do — design, start, review, monitor or administer — and change it at any time from the Role permissions screen.

sla.title: SLAs on your calendar
sla.text: Set deadlines in hours or business days on your own working hours and holidays. NWFM sends a reminder before a deadline and escalates when it passes.

integrations.title: Connect your other systems
integrations.text: Call REST and SOAP services, send email and SMS, and wait for a webhook callback — with credentials kept out of the workflow and every delivery logged.

how.title: From process to running work in three steps
how.subtitle: Set it up once, then let NWFM carry every request and field task from start to sign-off.
how.step1Text: Draw the workflow, build the forms its steps and field tasks collect, and set what each role can do. Publish when it is ready.
how.step2Text: Requests land in the right group's inbox, and field tasks go to the team that covers their territory.
how.step3Text: Follow every request and task as it moves, with workload views, SLA reminders and escalations when something slips.

trust.title: Your data stays yours
trust.subtitle: Each organisation gets its own workspace and its own database — and decides who gets in.
trust.databaseText: Your workflow data is never mixed with another organisation's. Each workspace runs on its own database.
trust.byoText: Prefer to keep data on your own infrastructure? Connect your own SQL Server during signup.
trust.ssoText: Staff sign in with your organisation's identity provider over SAML, with role-based permissions inside.
trust.supportText: NWFM support can enter your workspace only when your administrator grants time-limited access, which can be revoked at any time.

faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know before you start.
faq.a1: Every workspace has its own database. We host it for you, or you can connect your own SQL Server when you sign up.
faq.a2: A workflow engine with a visual designer, a no-code form engine, task management for your field teams, live monitoring with a workload dashboard, and permissions you set for each role — all in one workspace, in Arabic and English.
faq.q3: How do field teams use NWFM?
faq.a3: Each field team has its own login code and sees the tasks for its territory. The team fills the task's form — with photos, files and location — and submits it. A supervisor approves it or returns it with a reason.
faq.q4: Can we control who sees and does what?
faq.a4: Yes. Each role — such as Supervisor, Monitor or Field Team — has its own permissions, which administrators switch on or off at any time. Staff can also sign in with your organisation's accounts over SAML single sign-on.
faq.a5: Yes. Every screen is available in Arabic and English, with a full right-to-left layout for Arabic. Each user can switch language at any time.
faq.q6: Can NWFM staff see our data?
faq.a6: Only when your administrator grants support access. That access is time-limited, records a reason, and can be revoked at any time.
faq.a7: Create a workspace, choose a plan and confirm your email. We prepare your workspace and give you its sign-in link.

tips.tenantStatus: Active workspaces serve their users. Suspended or Maintenance refuses every sign-in and request until the workspace is activated again. Data is never deleted.
tips.subscriptionStatus: Billing state. A suspended, expired or cancelled subscription, or a trial that has run out, stops service even when the workspace is Active.
tips.schema: The last database update applied to this workspace. A workspace behind the current release answers "unavailable" until it is migrated.
tips.migrateAll: Applies pending database updates to every active workspace in the background. Users may see brief errors while their workspace updates; results land in the audit log.
tips.addWorkspace: Creates a workspace with a hosted database straight away (no approval step). The administrator is e-mailed a temporary password and a set-password link.
tips.tenantKey: The workspace address (for example acme → acme.eye360…). It is used in every link and cannot be changed later.
tips.plan: Decides the trial length and the user, team and storage limits the workspace gets.
tips.editWorkspace: Change the workspace name, contact details, default language, single sign-on and extra host names.
tips.manageSubscription: Activate after payment, extend a trial, move to another plan (new limits) or suspend / cancel. Suspending or cancelling stops service for every user.
tips.statusSection: Turns the whole workspace on or off for all of its users. Nothing is deleted.
tips.activate: Opens the workspace to its users again.
tips.suspend: Blocks every user and request of this workspace within about a minute — for non-payment or abuse. Data is kept. A reason is required and recorded.
tips.maintenance: Blocks users while you work on the workspace, for example a database repair. Data is kept. A reason is required and recorded.
tips.migrate: Applies pending database updates to this workspace now. Its users may see brief errors while it runs.
tips.pendingMigrations: Database updates this release needs that the workspace database does not have yet. While any are pending the workspace answers "unavailable".
tips.connection: Where this workspace's database lives. The password stays hidden unless you reveal it.
tips.reveal: Shows the full connection string, including the database password. You must give a reason, and every reveal is written to the audit log.
tips.admins: The administrators inside this workspace. They manage its users, teams and settings from the workspace app.
tips.addAdmin: Creates another administrator and e-mails a temporary password plus a set-password link. Counts towards the plan's user limit.
tips.resendCredentials: Issues a new temporary password and set-password link and e-mails them. Any password or link sent earlier stops working.
tips.suspendAdmin: Stops this administrator from signing in. Other users are not affected. The last active administrator cannot be suspended.
tips.reactivateAdmin: Lets this administrator sign in again.
tips.adminStatus: Pending activation: still on the temporary password (or never set one). Suspended: cannot sign in.
tips.support: Lets the support team open the workspace as one of its users to troubleshoot. It needs an active grant from the workspace, and every session is audited on both sides.
tips.startSupport: Opens the workspace in a new tab as the chosen user. Everything you do there is done as that user and recorded in the workspace audit log.
tips.supportGrants: Permission the workspace gave the support team, with a scope and an expiry. Without an active grant no support session can start.
tips.supportTicket: Your support ticket reference. It is recorded in both the platform and the workspace audit logs.
tips.supportAsUser: Whose permissions the session uses. Leave empty to act as the first administrator.
tips.approveSignup: Accepts the request. A hosted-database signup starts provisioning immediately; a bring-your-own-database one moves on to the database step.
tips.retrySignup: Runs provisioning again from the last step that finished. Use it after fixing what made it fail.
tips.rejectSignup: Declines the request and e-mails the customer a polite notice. Your reason stays internal. This cannot be undone.
tips.signupStatus: Awaiting approval: e-mail confirmed, waiting for you. Awaiting database: the customer still has to give working database details. Failed: provisioning stopped — Retry resumes it.
tips.addPlan: Creates a plan that can be offered at signup or assigned to workspaces.
tips.planCode: Permanent identifier used in signup links and the API. Changing it breaks links that use the old code.
tips.trialDays: Free days a new subscription on this plan gets. 0 starts the subscription as Active straight away.
tips.maxUsers: Most accounts a workspace on this plan may have. Empty means unlimited. Lowering it never removes users; it only blocks adding new ones.
tips.maxTeams: Most field teams a workspace on this plan may have. Empty means unlimited.
tips.maxStorage: Storage for uploaded files, in GB. Empty means unlimited.
tips.planPublic: Offered on the public signup page. A non-public plan can still be assigned by staff.
tips.planActive: Inactive plans cannot be picked for new signups or plan changes. Workspaces already on the plan keep it.
tips.addServer: Registers a SQL Server that new hosted workspace databases are created on.
tips.serverConnection: A SQL login allowed to create databases and logins (dbcreator and securityadmin). Stored encrypted and never shown again.
tips.serverLimit: How many workspace databases may be created on this server. When it is full, new workspaces go to another active server.
tips.containedUsers: Creates each workspace's login inside its own database (a contained user) instead of on the server. The server must allow contained database authentication.
tips.serverActive: Only active servers receive new workspace databases. Databases already on the server keep working.
tips.addStaff: Creates a staff account for this console.
tips.staffRole: Platform admin can change everything. Support can view workspaces, signups and the audit log, and start support sessions.
tips.staffActive: Inactive staff cannot sign in to this console.
tips.sso: Lets the workspace's users sign in through their organisation's identity provider. While it is on, password sign-in is closed to everyone except administrators.
tips.hosts: Extra domain names that open this workspace, such as the customer's own domain. Its DNS must point to us.
tips.language: The default language of the workspace and of the e-mails it sends.
tips.contactEmail: Where platform notices for this workspace are sent. It does not change anyone's sign-in.
tips.verify: Signs in as the runtime login and checks it cannot administer this database, open another one or impersonate anyone.
tips.listedPublicly: Show this workspace on the landing page's sign-in list. Off unless the customer asks for it.
